variable_or_topic: [v1 CF-009] creep_law
values_as_printed: Creep-law forms differ across sources: power law of normalised stress for carnallite (Барях et al. eq. 6.1), exponential/power laws for interseam layers and roof convergence (Соловьев–Секунцов eqs 7.18, 7.34), Drucker–Prager strain-hardening creep (Беляков–Беликов, Abaqus), Abel hereditary kernel (normative methodology via Лебедева), Coble diffusion creep on geological time (Кудряшов).
assessment: Not contradictory values but different model families at different scales/materials; no single law is evidenced for ВКМ salt at massif scale. Physical World v1 keeps the creep law as a MODEL_CHOICE (RD-007) with power-law (BGRa-type) as the executable default and the family recorded as structural uncertainty.
impact_on_worldspec: carried over from physical_evidence_v1 (not re-adjudicated here)

[8], cited p.27) — λ≈1 has cited VKM-regional field support; Лебедева concludes both indicate a near-hydrostatic field and her models use hydrostatic stress in potash seams; (H-λ1) elastic uniaxial-strain ν/(1−ν) = 0.25–0.67; (H-λ4) Филатова §2.3: horizontal stresses 1.2–1.5·γH "тектоническое наследие региона" [23], secondary and untraced — documented, NOT adopted; Гремячин

The historical 'no effect in CASE 08' holds only for the K0 key of the weak superposition, which implicitly represents λ = ν/(1−ν) and cannot represent λ at all. | Not closed by one number: hypotheses kept separate (never averaged); PW v1 uses the envelope H-λ1/H-λ2/H-λ3; H-λ4 documented only; Kaiser-effect stress memory in creeping salt is questionable (H-λ2 caveat). OGS CASE 08: the K0 key has no effect in the weak superposition, which implicitly represents H-λ1; pass 4 uses an explicit-λ formulation (CASE 14); no effect in the weak-material superposition; −8 %/−13 % in the stress-free soft inclusion.
